statement: the trash entry folder is named '<yyyyMMdd-HHmmss>-<the `id` field of itemMetadata>'; the timestamp is minted at the moment of the move
reachability: LIVE — binder Delete on any item

statement: itemMetadata carrying no `id` field — or that is not JSON at all — names the folder '<timestamp>-x'; the decode is best-effort and never fails the move
reachability: UNTRACED — every production caller encodes a StructureItem/ResearchItem or supplies an explicit id

statement: the file is MOVED out of the project tree into the entry folder, keeping its filename and its bytes; the original path is left empty; nothing is unlinked
reachability: LIVE — binder/research Delete on any file-backed item

statement: a group's FOLDER moves wholesale, subtree intact and nested structure preserved, in one FileManager.moveItem
reachability: LIVE — binder Delete on a group

statement: meta.json records originalRelativePath, displayTitle, itemMetadata, originalParentId and originalIndex, pretty-printed with sorted keys, written atomically
reachability: LIVE

statement: the TrashEntry moveToTrash RETURNS omits originalParentId and originalIndex (nil / 0) although meta.json and TrashStore.list() both carry the caller's values; the same entry read two ways is unequal
reachability: LIVE, but the returned entry is consumed only for its `id` — deleteStructureItem and deleteResearchItems both re-read the pane from list()

statement: an absolute, root-escaping, empty or empty-component fileRelativePath is refused with TrashError.unsafeRelativePath wrapping the SafeRelativePath.PathError, before any file is touched
reachability: LIVE for the empty case (a path-less manifest row, M3-TR-034); the hostile cases need a corrupted manifest

statement: a refused move still leaves the entry folder it created moments earlier: an empty directory under .trash/ with no file and no meta.json
reachability: LIVE via M3-TR-034

statement: a moveToTrash that throws leaves no meta.json, so the folder it created is invisible to list() and to every surface built on it
reachability: LIVE via M3-TR-034

statement: a source path that resolves safely but does not exist throws the raw NSCocoaErrorDomain error from FileManager, not a TrashError
reachability: LATENT — needs the manifest and the filesystem to disagree

statement: two moveToTrash calls in the same second under the same metadata id get DISTINCT entry folders: the second claims a uniquified name (<stamp>-<id>-2), both meta.json files survive and list() reports both deletions
reachability: UNTRACED — production ids are minted unique elsewhere; the guard is now local to this module as well

statement: restoring one of two same-second entries returns exactly its own file and leaves the other entry, folder and file untouched; each restore consumes only its own entry
reachability: UNTRACED — reachable only through M3-TR-011

statement: a project with no .trash directory lists as empty and does not throw
reachability: LIVE — every project open

statement: entries are returned sorted by trashedAt descending, newest first
reachability: LIVE — the Trash pane

statement: an entry whose meta.json is absent or undecodable is LISTED, labelled 'Unreadable entry (contents preserved)' with isUnreadable == true, and its contents stay on disk; a folder whose name Maugham did not write (M3-TR-016) and a folder holding nothing but unreadable metadata are still skipped
reachability: LATENT — a crash, force-quit or write failure between the move and the meta write produces exactly this state

statement: an entry folder whose name has no parseable 'yyyyMMdd-HHmmss' prefix is omitted from the list
reachability: UNTRACED from inside Maugham — every minted name parses; reachable by renaming the folder in Finder

statement: a non-directory file sitting at the .trash root is ignored entirely
reachability: UNTRACED from inside Maugham

statement: originalParentId and originalIndex round-trip through meta.json into the listed TrashEntry
reachability: LIVE

statement: sweep removes every listed entry whose trashedAt is more than 30 days old, destroying the folder and its contents
reachability: LIVE — ProjectStore.load calls sweep on every project open

statement: an entry 29 days old survives the sweep; the retention window is a full 30 days from the moment of deletion
reachability: LIVE

statement: sweep() walks the trash DIRECTORY: an entry whose meta.json never landed is aged by its folder-name timestamp, else its oldest filesystem date, and destroyed on schedule — the invisible-immortal entry is gone; an entry nothing can date is left alone
reachability: LATENT — same window as M3-TR-015

statement: sweep on a project with no .trash directory is a no-op and creates nothing
reachability: LIVE

statement: the parser reads the first two dash-separated fields as 'yyyyMMdd-HHmmss' and ignores everything after them; two folder names differing only after the second field parse to the same instant
reachability: LIVE

statement: a name with fewer than two dash-separated fields, or whose first two fields are not a valid date, parses to nil
reachability: LIVE

statement: the stamp format is 'yyyyMMdd-HHmmss' in TimeZone.current with no zone designator in the string, so a folder written in one zone reads as a different instant in another; the drift is bounded by the UTC offset
reachability: LIVE for a travelling writer; the effect is at most one day of 'days remaining' or of sweep timing

statement: restore moves the file back to meta.originalRelativePath, deletes the entry folder, and returns a TrashEntry that DOES carry originalParentId and originalIndex
reachability: LIVE — Trash pane Restore, and ⌘⌥Z

statement: a restore blocked by an occupant restores BESIDE it under a distinguishing name (numeric-suffix file dedupe; the binder row's title deduped ONLY when an occupant forced the rename) — both visible, nothing overwritten, nothing refused
reachability: LIVE — delete the last chapter, create a replacement (FileNaming reuses the freed NN and slug), then Restore

statement: an entry folder containing only meta.json throws TrashError.entryFileMissing, whose message names the real cause and lists what was actually in the folder
reachability: LATENT — needs the entry's file removed from inside .trash/

statement: an unknown trash id fails at the meta.json read as a raw NSCocoaErrorDomain error, not as a TrashError naming the entry
reachability: LATENT — needs a stale id, e.g. a second window that swept between refreshes

statement: a meta.json originalRelativePath that is absolute or escapes the project root is refused with TrashError.unsafeRelativePath and the entry is left intact
reachability: UNTRACED as a writer gesture — the guard exists for a corrupted or hostile sidecar

statement: restore creates the destination's intermediate directories, re-creating a folder the writer had deleted in order to receive the file
reachability: LIVE

statement: restore validates the entry id BEFORE anything moves: a malformed id throws with the entry intact on disk — the words survive the failed restore whole
reachability: UNTRACED as a writer gesture — Maugham always mints a parseable name; reachable by renaming a trash folder in Finder

statement: a successful structure delete refreshes trashEntries from disk and sets lastDeletedTrashId to the new entry, arming ⌘⌥Z
reachability: LIVE

statement: a structure item whose path is nil or empty cannot be deleted: the empty path is refused by the path guard, the manifest row survives, and an empty entry folder is left in .trash/
reachability: UNTRACED — I did not establish that any production path mints a path-less StructureItem

statement: a research link is restorable like everything else: deleting it writes a carriesFile:false trash entry holding its metadata, and restore returns it to the research tree — the note/link inequality is dissolved, not labelled
reachability: LIVE — research context-menu Delete on a saved URL

statement: the armed deletion record is the GESTURE (TrashDeletion: ids + label), so a delete that produces no trash entry can no longer leave the token pointing at an earlier unrelated deletion — ⌘⌥Z restores the whole gesture or refuses with its reason
reachability: LIVE — one file-backed research delete, then a link delete, then ⌘⌥Z

statement: one delete gesture is one restore: a batch delete arms the whole gesture, 'Restore Last Deletion' returns all of it or refuses naming why, and never returns part while reporting nothing about the rest
reachability: LIVE — multi-select delete in the research pane

statement: a restored StructureItem is re-inserted under its recorded originalParentId at its recorded originalIndex, clamped to the parent's current child count
reachability: LIVE

statement: when the recorded parent no longer exists, the row AND the file land together at the tree's root — the binder shows where the file is
reachability: LATENT — needs the child deleted, then the parent, then the child restored, in that order

statement: a restore that returns less than was deleted names what it could not return, at the moment of the restore: restoreTrashEntry returns a TrashRestoreReport (unreturned titles + relocations) and both TrashView and the ⌘⌥Z path surface it
reachability: LATENT — needs a descendant's file removed from inside .trash/

statement: a restored item lands where the binder says it is: the destination is computed from where the ROW is going and the row's (and descendants') paths are rewritten to where the file actually landed
reachability: LIVE — delete any research note, then Restore or ⌘⌥Z. Every research restore, every time.

statement: no folder the writer deleted is silently re-created on disk to hold a restored file — the GAP-1 occupant is never manufactured
reachability: LIVE — delete any research folder, then Restore

statement: the writer's Trash lists the writer's deletions: internal artifacts are typed (TrashSubject.internalArtifact) and filtered from list(); an entry whose wiring cannot be put back refuses loudly instead of restoring a file and reporting success
reachability: LIVE — MCP set_piece_style / clear_piece_style write trash entries with itemMetadata {"id":"style-<name>"}

statement: restoreLastDeletion consumes the armed TrashDeletion when it restores the gesture it names
reachability: LIVE

statement: with no armed token the command is a silent no-op: no throw, no change, no signal of any kind
reachability: LIVE — ⌘⌥Z in a freshly opened window

statement: emptyTrash attempts every entry, counts the ones it could not destroy and throws ProjectStoreError.trashNotEmptied(undestroyed:total:); trashEntries is re-listed from disk first, so what survived is still in the pane and TrashView's catch fires
reachability: LATENT for the I/O-failure half (permissions, an open handle, a sync daemon)

statement: emptyTrash walks the trash DIRECTORY (TrashStore.entryFolderIds), so an entry written to .trash/ behind ProjectStore's back — including an internalArtifact the pane never showed — is destroyed with the rest and the emptied trash is empty on disk
reachability: LIVE and needs no I/O failure — MCP set_piece_style writes straight through TrashStore without refreshing ProjectStore.trashEntries

statement: the single-entry permanent delete DOES propagate its failure to the caller, where TrashView alerts on it
reachability: LIVE

statement: permanent destruction LEAVES the armed deletion in place so the next ⌘⌥Z refuses with its reason rather than silently doing nothing (RULING-40's refuse-and-say-why applied to the token)
reachability: LIVE

statement: no verb in this module removes a document's op log at .maugham/ops/<docId>.jsonl: it survives the move to trash, 'Permanently Delete', 'Empty Trash' and the 30-day sweep alike, with its contents unchanged
reachability: LIVE — the retention is certain on every path; whether the writer ever NOTICES is not

statement: opening a project sweeps expired trash before the window is on screen, and never arms lastDeletedTrashId; the sweep's own failure is discarded (`try?`)
reachability: LIVE — every project open

statement: a metaless entry whose folder name carries no timestamp is aged by its oldest filesystem date
reachability: LIVE

scope: TrashStore/ProjectStore+Trash — sweep leaves the undatable alone
statement: an entry nothing can date is left alone rather than guessed at
reachability: LIVE

statement: a second occupant advances the numeric suffix — the next free name, never an overwrite
reachability: LIVE

statement: a restored link carries its URL and title back into the research tree intact
reachability: LIVE

statement: a gesture partially destroyed refuses whole with the reason; nothing is partially restored
reachability: LIVE

statement: an entry with metadata of neither kind refuses to restore rather than reporting success wiring-free
reachability: LIVE

scope: TrashStore/ProjectStore+Trash — both rows visible and named apart
statement: a beside-the-occupant restore leaves two distinguishable binder rows
reachability: LIVE

statement: all three inbox promote paths send the original capture asset to the trash, typed .captureAsset — never off the disk
reachability: LIVE

statement: a restored capture asset returns as a file (re-ingest is RULING-14's, and sufficient)
reachability: LIVE

statement: a uniquified entry id keeps the timestamp PREFIX, so TrashStore.parseTimestamp and ageOfEntry date a collided entry from its folder name rather than falling back to the filesystem
reachability: RULING-4's fix must not cost RULING-39's: the sweep dates entries by parsing the folder name.

statement: restoring an entry whose meta.json cannot be read throws TrashError.entryMetadataUnreadable naming the entry, and leaves the folder and its contents on disk; an id that is not in the trash at all still fails as a plain Cocoa error (M3-TR-029)
reachability: RULING-7: a refusal names its real cause, and the two refusals are different causes.

statement: restoring an unreadable entry from the writer's surface throws trashEntryNotRewirable titled 'Unreadable entry (contents preserved)', saying Maugham's record cannot be read and the contents are still in the trash folder
reachability: RULING-7 at the surface the writer's Restore actually reaches.

statement: an unreadable entry is still permanently deletable by folder name; being visible does not make it immortal
reachability: RULING-39's bugs-are-still-bugs clause: a listed entry must still be disposable.
